# Top Skills for Development

> Discover 22 popular agent skills for development, with original GitHub repositories.

> For agents — how to use this catalog:
> When starting a task, fetch https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app/skills.json.
> Match the task to each skill's Use-when line and category, and pick at most 2 skills.
> Then follow the chosen skill's own repository install instructions, and start with its example prompt.
> Do not install every matching skill — pick the smallest set that covers the task.
> Do not invent an install command: if the repository does not state one, say so and stop.
> If no skill matches the task, use no skill from this catalog rather than forcing a match.

> Full catalog in structured form: skills.json — Short index: llms.txt — Star counts are a snapshot supplied for 29 Oct 2026.

## Workflow

How work moves from an idea to shipped code.

### Superpowers

- Category: Workflow · Level: Intermediate · Stars: 307,155 · Repo: https://github.com/obra/superpowers · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-1
- Description: A comprehensive library of proven techniques for a stronger, more reliable coding agent workflow.
- Use when: At the start of a new task, before any code, when you want spec brainstorming, worktree isolation, bite-sized planning, and test-driven development.
- Top inside: Top inside: brainstorming, using-git-worktrees
- Inside: Inside this repo — 5 of 15 skills
- brainstorming [Planning] — Explores and clarifies user requirements through iterative questioning before building begins, synthesizing understanding into a written design specification.
  > Help me brainstorm the requirements and architecture for our new user authentication system before we write any code.
- using-git-worktrees [Setup] — Provisions an isolated development workspace on a separate branch using harness-native tooling or git worktree fallbacks, verifying clean baseline test status before implementation starts.
  > Set up an isolated git worktree on a new feature branch and verify a clean test baseline before starting work.
- writing-plans [Planning] — Decomposes an approved design document into granular, bite-sized tasks (2–5 minutes each) specifying exact file paths, full code implementations, and explicit test verification steps.
  > Create a granular implementation plan with bite-sized tasks, exact file paths, and test verification steps for our approved design.
- subagent-driven-development [Building] — Coordinates implementation by dispatching an isolated subagent for each task, followed by two-stage reviews (spec compliance and code quality) after every step.
  > Execute the plan in docs/superpowers/plans/auth-system.md using subagent-driven development, dispatching fresh subagents with reviews for each task.
- test-driven-development [Testing] — Enforces a strict Red-Green-Refactor discipline that requires writing a failing test and observing it fail before producing the minimal code required to pass.
  > Implement the user profile service using strict test-driven development by writing a failing test first before adding production code.

### ECC

- Category: Workflow · Level: Advanced · Stars: 291,489 · Repo: https://github.com/affaan-m/ECC · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-2
- Description: An agent-harness optimisation system with skills, memory, security practices, and research-first workflows.
- Use when: When running a full-lifecycle workflow in a supported harness that needs planning, test-driven implementation, fresh-context review, and build repair.
- Top inside: Featured: tdd-workflow, /ecc:plan
- Inside: Featured skills and commands
- tdd-workflow [Testing] — Directs a complete test-driven development cycle requiring a failing test prior to code implementation, followed by incremental greening and refactoring targeting 80%+ test coverage across unit, integration, and E2E suites.
  > Reproduce the shopping cart checkout bug with a failing test first, then use tdd-workflow to implement the fix.
- /ecc:plan [Planning] — Clarifies user requirements, assesses architectural and operational risks, and structures a step-by-step implementation plan while halting for explicit confirmation before code edits occur.
  > /ecc:plan "Implement user authentication with JWT tokens, role-based access control, and password reset endpoints in our API."
- /code-review [Review] — Conducts a structured, fresh-context code review on uncommitted local modifications or GitHub pull requests using a multi-phase checklist for bugs, style, and security.
  > /code-review Run a fresh-context review on uncommitted local modifications to check for bugs, styling issues, and potential security vulnerabilities.
- /build-fix [Debugging] — Inspects the repository to detect its active build system and iteratively resolves compiler, linter, and type-check errors using minimal, localized changes.
  > /build-fix Inspect the repository build system and incrementally resolve all TypeScript compiler and linter errors using minimal, localized changes.
- security-scan [Review] — Scans the agent harness setup (`.claude/` directory, MCP servers, hooks, and prompt guidelines) for configuration flaws, injection vulnerabilities, and credential exposure using AgentShield.
  > /security-scan .claude/ to audit our configuration for hardcoded secrets, injection vulnerabilities, and overly permissive MCP server settings.
- Note: Featured entries, not the whole catalog.

### Matt Pocock Skills

- Category: Workflow · Level: Intermediate · Stars: 305,511 · Repo: https://github.com/mattpocock/skills · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-4
- Description: Skills for real engineers, including alignment interviews and disciplined test-driven loops.
- Use when: At the start of feature or bug work, when human grilling should settle ambiguity and shared terminology before tickets and test-driven development.
- Top inside: Top inside: grill-with-docs, grill-me
- Inside: Inside this repo — 27 skills
- grill-with-docs [Planning] — Interrogates the user in depth about planned changes while writing Architecture Decision Records (ADRs) and maintaining a ubiquitous project domain glossary (`GLOSSARY.md`) before work starts.
  > /grill-with-docs Interview me about our proposed caching architecture while recording architectural decision records and updating our project glossary.
- grill-me [Planning] — Recursively interviews the user on an idea, plan, or general proposal until every branch of the design decision tree is explored and aligned.
  > /grill-me Interview me relentlessly about my proposal for a team on-call rotation until every branch of the plan is resolved.
- to-spec [Planning] — Turns a grilled understanding into a written specification, with implementation seams agreed up front before tickets are cut. (Source: skills/engineering/to-spec/SKILL.md, description + Process steps 2–3; orchestrator-verified 2026-10-29.)
  > /to-spec Turn our conversation into a complete feature specification, proposing test seams and publishing it to our issue tracker.
- implement [Building] — Executes tasks defined by a specification or ticket list, triggering `/tdd` across identified seams and terminating with `/code-review` before committing changes.
  > /implement Build the feature described in ticket #104, using test-driven development at identified seams and running code review before committing.
- code-review [Review] — Performs a dual-axis evaluation of repository diffs comparing code against standards and against the originating spec using parallel, isolated subagents.
  > Review our current changes since main against repo coding standards and originating issue #45 using parallel subagents for evaluation.
- ask-matt [Discovery] — Routes user to the right workflow or skill
  > Use ask-matt to recommend the best skill sequence for turning our auth refactor idea into tested, production-ready code.
- codebase-design [Planning] — Designs deep modules behind simple seams
  > Use codebase-design to restructure our payment gateway into a deep module hiding its internal webhook handlers behind one interface.
- diagnosing-bugs [Debugging] — Disciplined loop for hard bugs and failures
  > Use diagnosing-bugs to build a reproducible failing test for the intermittent session timeout before attempting any speculative code fix.
- domain-modeling [Planning] — Sharpens terms and updates glossary and ADRs
  > Use domain-modeling to clarify our order fulfillment terminology, resolve naming ambiguities, and update the glossary with our new state transitions.
- implement-spec [Building] — Executes full spec using concurrent workers
  > Use implement-spec to execute our completed billing integration spec across parallel implementer subagents on a dedicated feature branch.
- improve-codebase-architecture [Understanding] — Finds deep module opportunities in a codebase
  > Use improve-codebase-architecture to scan our repository for shallow abstractions, generate an interactive HTML report, and suggest deeper seams.
- pr [Writing] — Formats PR body with summary and verification
  > Use pr to construct a pull request description including a concise summary, before-and-after verification evidence, and merge risk analysis.
- prototype [Building] — Builds throwaway logic or UI spike prototypes
  > Use prototype to build a throwaway single-file HTML spike validating our multi-step checkout state machine before writing production code.
- research [Research] — Investigates primary sources into repo docs
  > Use research to investigate the latest Stripe webhook idempotency guidelines against official documentation and document findings in our repository.
- retro [Review] — Reviews session to improve agent environment
  > Use retro to evaluate our recent development session and recommend high-impact improvements to our linter rules, steering docs, and harness.
- setup-matt-pocock-skills [Setup] — Configures tracker, labels, and doc structure
  > Use setup-matt-pocock-skills to configure our GitHub issue tracker integration, establish triage labels, and initialize our domain documentation layout.
- tdd [Testing] — Drives red-green-refactor vertical slices
  > Use tdd to implement our token verification logic by writing a failing test first, followed by minimal implementation and refactoring.
- to-tickets [Planning] — Splits specs into tracer-bullet issue graphs
  > Use to-tickets to decompose our authentication specification into tracer-bullet tickets declaring explicit dependency edges for our tracking system.
- triage [Planning] — Processes issues into actionable agent briefs
  > Use triage to inspect incoming user bug reports, verify reproduction steps, apply triage labels, and draft structured agent-ready implementation briefs.
- wayfinder [Planning] — Maps multi-session work as decision tickets
  > Use wayfinder to break our database migration into a decision map of sequential tickets resolving unknowns one step at a time.
- wizard [Setup] — Generates interactive bash setup walkthroughs
  > Use wizard to generate an interactive bash script that guides our DevOps engineer step-by-step through manual AWS credential provisioning.
- grilling [Planning] — Relentless interview primitive for decisions
  > Use grilling to relentlessly interview me about our proposed caching strategy until every trade-off and edge case is thoroughly resolved.
- handoff [Communication] — Compacts session context for another agent
  > Use handoff to summarize our current debugging progress into a concise state document so another agent can continue the task seamlessly.
- teach [Communication] — Interactive workspace for learning concepts
  > Use teach to guide me through understanding distributed consensus algorithms with interactive exercises and incremental knowledge checks in this workspace.
- to-questionnaire [Planning] — Turns blocked decisions into questionnaires
  > Use to-questionnaire to create an asynchronous markdown questionnaire for our product manager regarding unresolved user permission requirements and trade-offs.
- wait-what [Communication] — Re-explains unclear messages using glossary
  > Use wait-what to rephrase your previous technical explanation in plain English using terminology already established in our project glossary.
- writing-for-agents [Writing] — Guides authoring docs and steering for agents
  > Use writing-for-agents to craft clear, concise instructions for our team steering guidelines following proven context-pointer and front-loading principles.

### Spec Kit

- Category: Workflow · Level: Intermediate · Stars: 143,671 · Repo: https://github.com/github/spec-kit · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-12
- Description: A toolkit for spec-driven development that helps agents build from a specification.
- Use when: When building a greenfield app or complex multi-step feature whose requirements and tasks must become executable specifications before code is generated.
- Top inside: Top commands: speckit-specify, speckit-plan
- Inside: Inside this repo — 5 core commands
- speckit-specify [Planning] — Creates or updates a detailed feature specification (`spec.md`) from natural language requirements, defining functional scope, user stories, and technical constraints.
  > /speckit-specify Build a photo organizer with albums grouped by date and a tile preview of each album.
- speckit-plan [Planning] — Executes implementation planning using design templates to generate technical design artifacts, technology choices, and architectural boundaries.
  > /speckit-plan Use .NET Aspire with Postgres, Blazor Server for the drag-and-drop frontend, and REST APIs for task management.
- speckit-tasks [Planning] — Decomposes the architectural plan and specification into an actionable, dependency-ordered `tasks.md` checklist for systematic implementation.
  > /speckit-tasks Break down our technical plan into an actionable, dependency-ordered checklist in tasks.md for systematic feature implementation.
- speckit-implement [Building] — Executes the implementation plan by processing and building out each task defined in `tasks.md` with prerequisite validation checks.
  > /speckit-implement Implement only the Setup and Foundational phases: project scaffolding and the project/task data model with basic CRUD.
- speckit-converge [Review] — Audits the codebase against the spec, plan, and tasks, automatically appending any missing or incomplete work as new tasks to `tasks.md` until full convergence is reached.
  > /speckit-converge Audit our codebase against the spec, plan, and tasks, appending any missing requirements to tasks.md until fully converged.

### Vercel Skills

- Category: Workflow · Level: Intermediate · Stars: 37,031 · Repo: https://github.com/vercel-labs/skills · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-16
- Description: An open agent skills tool installed with npx skills.
- Use when: When you need one CLI to search, install, update, sync, or test-run skills across several coding agent harnesses from git, URLs, or npm.
- Top inside: Top commands: find-skills, skills add
- Inside: Inside this repo — 1 skill, 4 commands
- find-skills [Discovery] — Instructs an AI coding agent on how to query and install agent skills via the Skills CLI when a user requests capabilities not natively supported.
  > Find a skill for building responsive HTML emails and install it directly into our current project workspace to style newsletters.
- skills add (command) [Setup] — Downloads and installs agent skills from GitHub repositories, URLs, or local paths directly into the active project or globally.
  > skills add vercel-labs/agent-skills --skill web-design-guidelines to configure our project with responsive layout rules and typography standards.
- skills find (command) [Discovery] — Interactively searches the open agent skills ecosystem by keyword query or scopes results to a specific GitHub owner.
  > skills find react performance --owner vercel-labs to discover verified optimization skills for our frontend application codebase.
- skills use (command) [Setup] — Generates prompt text or temporarily initializes a coding agent with a specified skill without permanently adding it to project dependencies.
  > skills use vercel-labs/agent-skills@web-design-guidelines to temporarily load styling rules into this agent session without installing them permanently.
- skills update (command) [Setup] — Checks for and updates installed project and global skills to their latest upstream releases.
  > skills update to refresh all installed agent skills to their latest upstream versions and check for breaking configuration changes.

### pstack

- Category: Workflow · Level: Advanced · Stars: 14,487 · Repo: https://github.com/cursor/plugins/tree/main/pstack · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-20
- Description: Poteto's official Cursor plugin that turns Cursor into a real engineering team, helping you write less but higher quality code with rigorous engineering principles and fearless parallelism via /poteto-mode and its 23 playbooks.
- Use when: At the start of a demanding task such as reproducing defects, tracing performance bottlenecks, or overnight autonomous work needing empirical verification.
- Top inside: Top inside: bug-fix, feature
- Inside: Inside this repo — 23 playbooks
- bug-fix [Debugging] — Mandates reproducing a reported defect directly on the matching target surface first, binary-searching root causes with runtime evidence, and staging a failing repro test commit before landing the fix.
  > /poteto-mode users get two notifications after a retry: repro first with a failing test, then fix and verify.
- feature [Building] — Orchestrates implementing new or modified behavior by establishing domain data shapes, conducting parallel architectural exploration, writing a four-dimension throughput checkpoint, and delegating scoped implementation.
  > /poteto-mode Implement webhook signature verification for inbound Stripe events, establishing domain data shapes and throughput checkpoints before delegating scoped code changes.
- investigation [Understanding] — Executes read-only inquiry into how a subsystem functions or why an architectural decision was made, producing cited explanations and tradeoff matrices without introducing code modifications.
  > /poteto-mode Investigate how our session expiration and token refresh pipeline works, providing cited code explanations and tradeoff analysis without modifying any files.
- refactoring [Building] — Performs behavior-preserving structural alterations by first pinning existing contracts with characterization tests, eliminating dead code, and migrating callers and legacy APIs simultaneously in a single wave.
  > /poteto-mode Refactor the legacy billing service into modular handlers, pinning existing behavior with characterization tests first to ensure zero functional regressions.
- perf-issue [Debugging] — Traces measured slowness against an established baseline trace, systematically applies performance mantras in order of cost, and independently verifies post-fix metric improvements before shipping.
  > /poteto-mode Trace database query latency on the dashboard endpoint against our baseline profile and optimize the slow queries with verified post-fix benchmarks.
- authoring-a-skill [Writing] — Owns a skill’s voice by validating frontmatter, referenced files, cross-skill links, and structural test cases, deleting prose that changes no decision, then running Opening a PR.
  > /poteto-mode Author a release-notes skill with valid frontmatter, working cross-skill links, and structural cases, keeping only instructions that change decisions.
- autonomous-run [Planning] — Defines a checkable exit condition, then drives toward it without stopping through evidence-based iterations, event watchers or timed heartbeats, verifying each change and discarding attempts that do not advance it.
  > /poteto-mode Run until the invoice retry regression passes consistently, defining the exit predicate first and using heartbeats to verify each attempted fix.
- autopilot-full [Review] — Owns verdicts while assigning one owner per PR, requiring independent verification by a swarm that never wrote the code and green CI at each current head before anything merges.
  > /poteto-mode Coordinate the three billing PRs with one owner each, independent verification swarms, and green CI at each head before allowing merges.
- autopilot-stack [Review] — Runs Autopilot-full verification without merging, stopping at verified PRs with green checks at their current heads and handing them to the operator, stacking only PRs that build on others.
  > /poteto-mode Verify the schema and billing migration PRs as a dependent stack, then hand their current-head verdicts to me without merging.
- babysit [Review] — Owns the merge frontier by declaring a mode, clearing one PR at a time, and stopping where a human decision begins, while leaving the actual landing operation to Shipping.
  > /poteto-mode Babysit the completed invoice PR stack in drive mode, clearing one PR at a time and stopping when a product decision needs me.
- eval [Testing] — Owns experiment design through planning, blinding, running, and synthesising results, keeping evaluation language out of candidate environments and prompts while a blinded judge assesses outputs against a private rubric.
  > /poteto-mode Evaluate two release-note instruction variants with sanitized workspaces, one organic task, and a blinded judge using a private rubric for factual accuracy.
- hillclimb [Testing] — Owns one metric and experiment integrity through a frozen measurement harness, testing one change at a time, keeping measured improvements or reverting failures, and never claiming wins from inspection alone.
  > /poteto-mode Reduce dashboard startup latency with a frozen realistic workload, one change per measurement, and a decision log recording every kept or reverted attempt.
- multi-phase-plan [Planning] — Owns the plan rather than implementation, producing an evidence-backed checklist an owner executes box by box and an operator audits, with dependencies, verification steps, and explicit review gates.
  > /poteto-mode Plan the billing provider migration as ordered PR checklists with dependencies, evidence requirements, and review gates, without implementing any code.
- opening-a-pr [Communication] — Runs at the end of every other playbook, preparing work in a worktree off main and organising small ordered commits so each can become a future independently landable PR.
  > /poteto-mode Prepare the invoice retry fix for review from a worktree off main, arranging small ordered commits that each form a landable PR.
- orchestrate [Planning] — Runs the program rather than writing code, deciding which agent owns each piece, checking the evidence each produces, and maintaining authoritative program state in the Project tracker throughout execution.
  > /poteto-mode Coordinate the checkout migration across scoped agent owners, check their evidence, and maintain dependencies and progress in the Project tracker.
- pause-safely [Planning] — Owns a clean stop by finishing or backing out of the atomic step, taking no irreversible action, and leaving a durable wip checkpoint with a resume note for a cold-start agent.
  > /poteto-mode Pause the checkout migration at a safe boundary, checkpoint unfinished work, and record verified progress, current state, and the first action for resumption.
- prototype [Design] — Owns a design decision through a throwaway instrument, exploring alternatives quickly in an isolated scratch directory, observing their behaviour, and handing the chosen direction to Feature for the real build.
  > /poteto-mode Prototype compact and spacious invoice tables behind a switcher in a scratch directory, observe their interactions, and recommend a direction for Feature.
- runtime-forensics [Debugging] — Owns diagnosis from a live process by capturing a profile, heap snapshot, or CDP trace, reducing it to the smoking gun, and proving the mechanism before delivering a cited diagnosis.
  > /poteto-mode Capture a heap snapshot from the running invoice dashboard, trace retained subscriptions to their GC roots, and deliver a cited diagnosis before proposing fixes.
- session-pickup [Understanding] — Owns the resume point by reading the prior transcript, cloud URL, or pushed branch first, reconstructing completed and pending work without redoing it, and retaining a reduced timeline in the main thread.
  > /poteto-mode Resume the invoice migration from its pushed branch and prior transcript, identify completed work and pending decisions, and continue from the recorded resume point.
- shipping [Review] — Owns what lands by verifying each PR independently, landing only the verified contiguous run from the root, confirming each merge, and keeping hands off the stack while it lands.
  > /poteto-mode Ship the verified billing stack from its root through its approved ceiling, confirming each merge and preserving the remaining stack while it lands.
- trace-forensics [Debugging] — Owns diagnosis from an existing artifact by identifying its format, parsing it with generic tooling, reducing it to a source-attributed finding, and distinguishing confirmed causes from hypotheses without a live rerun.
  > /poteto-mode Analyze the saved checkout CPU profile with a generic parser, identify the hot call path and source symbols, and report the strongest supported diagnosis.
- visual-parity [Testing] — Owns pixel-exact equivalence by establishing the baseline before migration, moving one component at a time, and verifying zero image diff without changing the harness or tampering with baseline images.
  > /poteto-mode Migrate the invoice status component against its existing screenshot baseline, checking every state by image diff and preserving the harness and baseline images.
- worktree-cleanup [Setup] — Snapshots and audits worktrees and simulator state using paths from worktree list, classifying size, age, merge state, uncommitted work, and PR state before checking active usage and pruning confirmed candidates.
  > /poteto-mode Audit worktrees and simulator storage, classify candidates from worktree list, cross-check active chats, and hold any uncommitted work for my decision.

## Quality

Checks that keep code honest before it ships.

### Karpathy Skills

- Category: Quality · Level: Beginner · Stars: 225,828 · Repo: https://github.com/multica-ai/andrej-karpathy-skills · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-3
- Description: A single behaviour guide distilled from common LLM coding pitfalls.
- Use when: During a non-trivial coding task where models tend to assume silently, add speculative abstractions, edit unrelated code, or skip verifiable test loops.
- Top inside: Inside: karpathy-guidelines
- Inside: Inside this repo — the only skill
- karpathy-guidelines [Planning] — Enforces four foundational behavioral principles (Think Before Coding, Simplicity First, Surgical Changes, and Goal-Driven Execution) to curb AI over-engineering, unstated assumptions, and extraneous edits.
  > Follow the karpathy-guidelines to add a feature to export user data, clarifying assumptions and delivering minimal surgical changes with verified tests.

### Agent Skills

- Category: Quality · Level: Advanced · Stars: 111,372 · Repo: https://github.com/addyosmani/agent-skills · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-8
- Description: Production-grade engineering skills for AI coding agents.
- Use when: When guiding an agent through multi-stage feature delivery that needs requirements, specs, tests, security passes, and human checkpoints to prevent shortcuts.
- Top inside: Top inside: /spec, /plan
- Inside: Inside this repo — 5 of 25 skills
- /spec [Planning] — Authors a comprehensive PRD covering objectives, commands, directory structure, testing strategy, and boundaries before writing any code.
  > /spec Author a complete product requirements document for adding role-based access control with admin permissions and audit logging before implementation.
- /plan [Planning] — Decomposes specifications into small, atomic, verifiable implementation tasks ordered by dependency with clear acceptance criteria.
  > /plan Decompose our user authentication specification into small, atomic implementation tasks ordered by dependency with explicit acceptance criteria.
- /build [Building] — Implements changes in vertical slices—coding, testing, verifying, and committing atomically with safe defaults and feature flags.
  > /build Implement the user registration slice from our plan, writing tests and verifying functionality before committing each change atomically.
- /test [Testing] — Enforces a strict Red-Green-Refactor cycle following the test pyramid to verify functional correctness and prevent regressions.
  > /test Apply a strict Red-Green-Refactor cycle to implement input validation for email signups, writing failing tests first before production code.
- /review [Review] — Conducts a five-axis pre-merge quality and code health review evaluating architecture, correctness, tests, security, and maintainability.
  > /review Conduct a five-axis pre-merge review of our authentication pull request, evaluating correctness, architecture, tests, security, and maintainability.

## Design

Interfaces that look considered, not generated.

### UI/UX Pro Max

- Category: Design · Level: Intermediate · Stars: 141,949 · Repo: https://github.com/nextlevelbuilder/ui-ux-pro-max-skill · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-5
- Description: Design intelligence for professional, polished user interfaces.
- Use when: When building, refactoring, or auditing an interface that needs concrete choices on palette, font pairing, responsive layout, and accessibility compliance.
- Top inside: Top inside: ui-ux-pro-max, design-system
- Inside: Inside this repo — 5 of 7 skills
- ui-ux-pro-max [Design] — Delivers searchable, stack-specific design intelligence across 22 frameworks, covering UI styles, color palettes, font pairings, animations, and UX best practices.
  > Build a landing page for my SaaS product with dark mode, modern typography pairings, and accessible shadcn/ui components.
- design-system [Design] — Generates multi-tiered design token architectures (primitive, semantic, component), CSS variables, component specifications, and presentation slide structures.
  > Generate a complete design system for our analytics dashboard, establishing primitive, semantic, and component token layers with CSS variables.
- ui-styling [Design] — Directs the creation of accessible web interfaces utilizing shadcn/ui components, Tailwind CSS utility patterns, and visual canvas layouts.
  > Style our user settings dashboard using accessible shadcn/ui components, responsive Tailwind CSS utility classes, and custom dark mode themes.
- design [Design] — Coordinates broad branding and graphic deliverables, including logo creation, corporate identity programs, social cards, mockups, and icon generation.
  > Design a complete brand identity package including modern SVG vector icons, social preview cards, and corporate presentation slide templates.
- banner-design [Design] — Designs responsive digital and print banners across social platforms, display advertising, and website hero sections using preset art direction styles.
  > Create a set of responsive promotional banners for our product launch across Twitter, LinkedIn, and website hero sections using glassmorphism styling.

### Impeccable

- Category: Design · Level: Intermediate · Stars: 94,446 · Repo: https://github.com/pbakaus/impeccable · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-22
- Description: The design vocabulary for your coding agent, steering with polish and bolder, reviewing with critique and audit, and catching AI slop before it ships.
- Use when: When designing, critiquing, polishing, or auditing frontend interfaces to elevate craft and catch AI design slop before shipping.
- Top inside: Top commands: init, polish
- Inside: Inside this repo — 23 commands
- init [Planning] — Runs project discovery once per project, asking only what it cannot infer, and writes PRODUCT.md that every later command reads.
  > Run /impeccable init for this project, discovering its users, jobs, and constraints and writing the PRODUCT.md every later command will read.
- polish [Design] — Refines an existing interface for shipping without redesigning it, fixing blockers, missing states, drift, and visual inconsistencies in priority order.
  > /impeccable polish the settings page, refining it for shipping without redesigning it and fixing missing states and visual inconsistencies first.
- bolder [Design] — Amplifies a safe or bland interface to the conviction the rest of the design system already implies, scoped to the named target only.
  > /impeccable bolder the pricing cards, amplifying their hierarchy and visual conviction without rebuilding the surrounding page or adding effects.
- critique [Review] — Scores a design against usability heuristics with dual isolated assessments and detector evidence, ranking what to fix first.
  > /impeccable critique the pricing cards, scoring the design against usability heuristics and ranking the fixes that matter most first.
- audit [Review] — Checks accessibility, performance, theming, responsive behaviour, and implementation integrity, ranking findings P0 (blocking) to P3 (polish).
  > Run /impeccable audit on the checkout flow, checking accessibility, performance, theming, and responsive behaviour and ranking findings from P0 to P3.
- adapt [Design] — Adapts designs across screen sizes, devices, contexts, and platforms by implementing breakpoints, fluid layouts, and touch targets that keep responsive interfaces usable across different viewing conditions.
  > /impeccable adapt the appointment booking form for phones and tablets, adjusting breakpoints, fluid layouts, and touch targets throughout the flow.
- animate [Design] — Enhances a feature with purposeful animations, micro-interactions, and motion effects that improve usability and add delight, making transitions and interactions feel more alive without adding decoration for its own sake.
  > /impeccable animate the file upload panel with progress transitions and completion feedback that help users understand each stage of uploading.
- clarify [Writing] — Improves unclear UX copy, error messages, microcopy, labels, and instructions so interfaces become easier to understand, addressing confusing text and hard-to-follow guidance wherever users need clearer wording.
  > /impeccable clarify the password reset flow, rewriting its field labels, expired link message, and recovery instructions so users understand their next step.
- colorize [Design] — Adds strategic color to monochromatic features or interfaces that lack visual interest, making dull designs more engaging and expressive with a palette that brings warmth and vibrancy.
  > /impeccable colorize the gray meal planning dashboard, using strategic color to distinguish meal groups and make the weekly view more engaging.
- delight [Design] — Adds moments of joy, personality, and unexpected touches that make interfaces memorable and enjoyable to use, elevating functional experiences with details that give everyday interactions a more delightful character.
  > /impeccable delight the reading tracker with a memorable book completion moment and small touches of personality in its reading milestones.
- distill [Design] — Strips designs to their essence by removing unnecessary complexity, noise, and elements, simplifying crowded interfaces into cleaner, more focused experiences that retain a simple and powerful design.
  > /impeccable distill the subscription management screen, removing repeated explanations and unnecessary controls so the current plan and renewal action stand out.
- document [Writing] — Generates DESIGN.md in Google Stitch format by extracting colors, typography, spacing, radii, and component patterns from existing code, then confirms descriptive language for atmosphere and color character with the user.
  > /impeccable document the existing travel planner design system in DESIGN.md, extracting its visual patterns and confirming atmosphere and color descriptions with me.
- extract [Design] — Pulls reusable patterns, components, and design tokens into the design system, identifying repeated implementations and consolidating them to reduce drift and restore consistency across the codebase.
  > /impeccable extract the repeated account settings controls into shared components and design tokens, consolidating spacing and field patterns across the settings screens.
- generate [Design] — Boots live mode, finds the named element on the open page, scrolls to it, and delivers the requested number of design variants for the user to cycle through and accept.
  > /impeccable generate 3 restrained variants of the membership comparison cards, bringing the named element into view so I can cycle through and accept one.
- harden [Building] — Makes interfaces production-ready through error handling, internationalization, text overflow fixes, and edge case management, improving resilience when real-world data and unusual input put existing screens under pressure.
  > /impeccable harden the delivery address form for long international addresses, translated labels, failed submissions, and incomplete customer data before release.
- layout [Design] — Improves layout, spacing, and visual rhythm by fixing monotonous grids, inconsistent spacing, and weak hierarchy, giving crowded or poorly aligned interfaces a clearer and more coherent composition.
  > /impeccable layout the inventory overview, fixing its monotonous grid, crowded stock summaries, and inconsistent spacing so the most urgent information leads.
- live [Design] — Starts interactive live variant mode on a running dev server, letting users select browser elements and design actions while AI-generated HTML and CSS alternatives hot-swap through HMR.
  > /impeccable live on the running dev server so I can select the event header in the browser and compare alternative design actions.
- onboard [Design] — Designs onboarding flows, first-run experiences, and empty states that guide new users to value through welcome screens, account setup, progressive disclosure, contextual guidance, and meaningful activation moments.
  > /impeccable onboard new users of the shared grocery list, designing the first empty state and setup steps through adding their first household item.
- optimize [Debugging] — Diagnoses and fixes UI performance across loading speed, rendering, animations, images, and bundle size, addressing slow or laggy interfaces to make the experience faster and smoother.
  > /impeccable optimize the photo archive grid, diagnosing slow image loading, rendering delays, and scrolling jank before fixing the largest performance costs.
- overdrive [Design] — Pushes interfaces past conventional limits with technically ambitious implementations such as shaders, spring physics, scroll-driven reveals, and 60fps animations, creating extraordinary experiences with strong visual impact.
  > /impeccable overdrive the astronomy exhibition opening with a shader starfield, spring interactions, and scroll-driven reveals that sustain smooth 60fps motion.
- quieter [Design] — Tones down visually aggressive or overstimulating designs by reducing intensity while preserving quality, giving overwhelming interfaces a calmer, more refined aesthetic when their current treatment feels too loud.
  > /impeccable quieter the concert ticket dashboard, reducing competing visual intensity so ticket status and entry details feel calm and easy to scan.
- shape [Planning] — Plans UX and UI before code through a discovery interview, using visual probes when available and producing a user-confirmed design brief that guides the subsequent implementation work.
  > /impeccable shape a volunteer shift signup flow, interviewing me about coordinator needs and confirming a design brief before any implementation begins.
- typeset [Design] — Improves typography by fixing font choices, hierarchy, sizing, weight, and readability, making interface text feel intentional and giving existing content a more polished and deliberate typographic treatment.
  > /impeccable typeset the recipe detail page, improving ingredient readability, instruction hierarchy, font sizing, and weight so cooks can follow each step easily.

## Efficiency

Less noise between thought and output.

### Caveman

- Category: Efficiency · Level: Beginner · Stars: 115,725 · Repo: https://github.com/JuliusBrussee/caveman · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-6
- Description: Concise, token-efficient agent communication.
- Use when: In interactive terminal coding sessions where replies pile up token waste, latency, and conversational filler.
- Top inside: Featured: /caveman, /ultracave
- Inside: Featured skills and commands
- /caveman [Communication] — Enforces an ultra-concise, structured communication style (answer first, one idea per sentence, eliminating conversational filler) while preserving code, file paths, commands, and numbers character-for-character.
  > /caveman explain why my React component re-renders every time the parent updates and how to memoize props without breaking state.
- /ultracave [Communication] — Compresses agent communication to maximum brevity using sentence fragments and single-word answers while stating each technical fact only once.
  > /ultracave diagnose why my long-running Node.js worker leaks memory and recommend minimal fixes without conversational pleasantries.
- /caveman-compress [Writing] — Shrinks agent steering and memory files (e.g., `CLAUDE.md`, `AGENTS.md`) to conserve context window tokens while backing up originals and keeping headings, code blocks, and paths intact.
  > /caveman-compress CLAUDE.md to shrink this project memory file and conserve context window tokens before starting development.
- /caveman-review [Review] — Performs a dense code review outputting exactly one finding per line anchored to code line numbers without discursive preambles.
  > /caveman-review the current pull request diff and output exactly one actionable finding per line with severity, location, and fix.
- investigate-first [Debugging] — Enforces a disciplined debugging playbook requiring the agent to gather log/test evidence and confirm a credible failure mechanism before any code edits are authorized.
  > Investigate the intermittent timeout failures in our payment service by tracing failure evidence and ranking hypotheses without modifying product code.
- Note: Featured entries, not the whole catalog.

## Knowledge

Ways to hold a codebase in your head.

### Graphify

- Category: Knowledge · Level: Intermediate · Stars: 137,533 · Repo: https://github.com/Graphify-Labs/graphify · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-7
- Description: Turns a codebase into an explorable knowledge graph.
- Use when: When exploring an unfamiliar codebase or a mixed folder of code, PDFs, notes, and images that needs a persistent, queryable graph of cross-file links.
- Top inside: Top subcommands: /graphify, graphify query
- Inside: Inside this repo — 1 skill, 4 subcommands
- /graphify [Understanding] — Executes the full deterministic AST parsing and extraction pipeline on a codebase to detect communities, identify god nodes, and generate an interactive HTML visual graph, GraphRAG-ready JSON, and a `GRAPH_REPORT.md` architecture summary.
  > /graphify . --mode deep to extract AST dependencies, identify god nodes, and generate the architecture report for this codebase.
- graphify query (subcommand) [Understanding] — Answers architecture and code relationship questions using deterministic graph traversal (BFS or semantic search) against local graph artifacts instead of grepping raw source files.
  > Run graphify query "what connects auth to the database?" using BFS traversal to trace component dependencies without reading raw files.
- graphify path (subcommand) [Understanding] — Traces and outputs the dependency and call connection paths between two specified components or god nodes within the knowledge graph.
  > Run graphify path "UserService" "DatabasePool" to trace all intermediary call chains and dependencies connecting these two components.
- graphify explain (subcommand) [Understanding] — Inspects a specific node or component in the graph and summarizes its architectural role, community membership, upstream dependencies, and downstream dependents.
  > Run graphify explain "RateLimiter" to summarize its architectural role, community membership, upstream dependencies, and downstream caller components.
- graphify add (subcommand) [Research] — Ingests, parses, or transcribes an external artifact (such as an arXiv paper URL, YouTube video, or document) and merges its extracted entities into the existing project graph.
  > Run graphify add https://arxiv.org/abs/1706.03762 to ingest this transformer architecture paper and merge its concepts into our graph.

### Understand-Anything

- Category: Knowledge · Level: Intermediate · Stars: 88,717 · Repo: https://github.com/Egonex-AI/Understand-Anything · Card: https://topskillsfordevelopment.vercel.app#skill-9
- Description: Turns any codebase into an interactive knowledge graph to explore, search, and ask questions about.

- Top inside: Top inside: understand, understand-dashboard
- Inside: Inside this repo — 5 of 9 skills

  > /understand to scan our project with tree-sitter, extract all dependencies, and generate the initial knowledge graph in .ua/.
- understand-dashboard [Understanding] — Launches an interactive, web-based visual dashboard displaying the codebase knowledge graph color-coded by architectural layer with search and inspection capabilities.
  > /understand-dashboard to launch the interactive web visualizer and inspect our project knowledge graph color-coded by architectural layer.
- understand-chat [Understanding] — Answers natural language architectural and flow questions about the project by traversing the indexed knowledge graph without reading entire raw files.
  > /understand-chat How does the payment flow work from user checkout down through the payment gateway and transaction logging?
- understand-diff [Understanding] — Evaluates git diffs and pending code modifications against the knowledge graph to determine structural impact, affected dependencies, and downstream blast radius.
  > /understand-diff to evaluate our uncommitted git modifications against the knowledge graph and report affected downstream components and risks.
- understand-explain [Understanding] — Performs a focused architectural breakdown of a specified file, class, or function, detailing its structural role, callers, callees, and dependencies.
  > /understand-explain src/auth/login.ts to break down its structural role, callers, callees, and imported dependencies across our codebase.

### Claude Skills Collection
